candidates.excerpt: The Port of Gdańsk handled 65.2 million tonnes of cargo between January and September 2026, compared with 59.1 million tonnes in the same period of 2025, an increase of more than 10%. General cargo, and containerised cargo in particular, accounted for the largest share of the growth. General cargo totalled 23.5 million tonnes, 3.6 million tonnes or 18 per cent more than a year earlier. Containerised cargo reached 21.1 million tonnes, up 17.6%, while container throughput rose 21% from just over 2 million to nearly 2.5 million TEUs. Coal handling grew 36 per cent to 6.7 million tonnes, an additional 1.8 million tonnes, and grain rose 33 per cent to 2.1 million tonnes, more than half a million tonnes above the previous year. The only category to decline was other bulk cargo, which fell 1.5 per cent to 2.8 million tonnes. candidates.title: ONE expands container reuse services to Switzerland with Avantida
candidates.excerpt: Ocean Network Express (ONE) has introduced container reuse services in Switzerland through its collaboration with Avantida, allowing transport operators to reuse import containers for export shipments. The service aims to reduce unnecessary empty container movements and improve the efficiency of inland logistics operations. Under the arrangement, transport companies can reuse eligible import containers for export cargo instead of returning them to a depot before collecting another empty unit. This process, commonly known as a street turn, can help reduce additional truck journeys, waiting times and transport costs. Improving inland container operations Through Avantida’s container reuse solution, ONE customers in Switzerland can explore opportunities to connect import and export container movements more efficiently. candidates.title: When the ship pays back before the owner does
candidates.excerpt: When the ship pays back before the owner does Fuel-saving retrofits can pay for themselves long before the shipowner who funded them sees a return. A new BIMCO contract seeks to resolve shipping’s longstanding divide between who pays for efficiency and who pockets the savings. Alex Byelyavtsev reports. DNV’s Maritime Forecast to 2050 has a 5,000 teu case: bow modification, propeller retrofit and propeller boss cap fin. About 16% fuel saving. Payback around one to four years, depending on fuel price. Industry coverage puts the package at about $2.35m. That calculation belongs to the ship. It does not say who receives the saving. On time charter the owner owns the vessel. The charterer typically buys the bunkers. If the owner pays to burn less, the immediate fuel saving shows up first in the charterer’s accounts. candidates.excerpt: A time for a change So, you want to build a railroad, but perhaps you’re having a hard time finding a dedicated space for a layout. Or maybe you have the space, but you lack the ability to work well with small details, such as those found on N and HO scale models. And perhaps you’d like a large railroad, but you’re just overwhelmed by the cost in time and resources to build one. If any or all of those concerns fit your situation, then consider building a narrow gauge O scale sectional layout, such as my Olympia & Sand Creek Ry. The layout, also known as just “Olympia,” was constructed in three distinct sections over a 12-year period. Each section contained its own set of approachable projects, spreading the cost and modeling work over time. candidates.excerpt: Schneider will make Norfolk Southern its primary eastern rail provider under an agreement announced Oct. 29 aimed at expanding domestic intermodal capacity and giving shippers more options to move freight across the eastern United States. The agreement, effective in November, shifts Schneider’s NYSE: SNDR) company-owned equipment, drivers and logistics operations away from CSX (NASDAQ: CSX) and pairs it with Norfolk Southern’s 22-state intermodal network. candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026. candidates.excerpt: Hengli Heavy Industry bags 52 ultra-large container ships LNG dual-fuel newbuilds bolster the shipbuilder’s container ship orderbook including large-scale contract from MSC Hengli Heavy Industry announced that it has recently secured shipbuilding contracts with several globally leading container liner operators, with a combined orderbook of 52 ultra-large dual-fuel container ships. The new container vessel portfolio comprises three primary variants: twenty 19,000 teu ships, twelve units of 22,000 teu ships and twenty 24,000 teu ships. Last week MSC contracted twenty 24,000 teu vessels with the Chinese shipbuilder. “Hengli Heavy Industry continues to deepen cooperation with major global liner and shipping groups, contributing to the green upgrading of global shipping across container, oil, dry bulk and emerging ammonia trades,” stated the shipyard.
